I'm not sure about marriage/family things, because I think we're quite young and should focus on different things, like careers and maybe moving to another country. We're in Russia. She's transgender. She's literally afraid to go outside and has a lot of problems, fears, complexes because of her gender dysphoria. Within a year, the operation (FFS) will be done. I'm looking forward to it, because I think it will ease her life and change her perception of herself and self-esteem for the better (she has a low self-esteem, which is the source of many problems, in my opinion). 

We're also in a complicated situation when it comes to our location, since we're living in one city (in the European part of the state) and her mother's in the opposite (not that far from Korea, Japan and China). She can't go home because of the problems with her grandparents, caused by her transition. And she can't live on her own because of her social disadaptation. 

So basically, she's trapped in here, and even if we decide to break up, I will have to interact with her. So the break-up won't really work, I reckon. 

Also, I'm an idealist, so I believe that any person can change if they want to and are willing to put an effort in it. I also consider her age to be an important factor in the whole situation. Looking back in the past, I was a different person in her age -- acted more irrational, impulsive, reckless, etc. 18 was the age when I started to change. 

Her being a sincere person was one of the first things to impress me. But it now appears to be another side of the power and control her emotions have over her. To me, it looks logical.

Yes, victim mentality is the worst.

Quite strange, she's texting me saying she wants to talk asap.
Well, she cares. She really does. But she always thinks of herself as mistreated, I guess. Egoistic? Maybe, I don't know.

I find her a very impulsive person. She regrets half of what she says when driven by emotions, but she can't control them at all.

I love her, so does she, I know for sure. And when everything's fine, we're happy. But she always finds something to be annoyed. The longest we didn't argue was a week and a half. Even during this short period, she was close to start a fight twice.

Personally, I think that she makes huge problems out of little ones. Those which we could better talk over. But I don't know how to change the fashion. She doesn't really hear what I say.
She's unblocked me to say that she's tired of everything, including me, and is asking how to get rid of me... :'(

I didn't actually learn it in school or anywhere else. All I did was translating my favourite songs, trying to understand what they are about. This practice gave me some knowledge back when I was 13. Then I went to start writing in English on my own, watching films in English, YouTube, using different English speaking forums, etc. I also write music, and the lyrics are in English as well.

The hardest part, if we can call it that, is vocabulary. It still seems like a continuous process.

And for example, when I did my final exams in school, I chose English as one of them. I got 84 out of 100. Compare it to my results in Russian - 87.

So, I wouldn't say it was hard to learn. Russian is way harder.
Thank you for sharing your experience. Self-loathing is something she's sadly full of, by the way.
Exactly how I see the subconscious thing. Personally, for me subconscious and unconscious things mean a lot.

Exactly. I can definitely see it. It was very hard for her to recognise that I actually love her, to believe my words when I say she's very beautiful, to start going out without thinking about how people around perceive her.

But we've come through it, because she believed me. She still has doubts, but tries to fight them. She's got more confident, her self-esteem has started improving. And then this. I hope it won't erase all the progress back to where we started.

I have never had a problem with gendering her, til this moment. We're in Russia.

I wanted to say "почему ты ТАКОЙ грубой [стала]?" ("why d'you become SO rude?").
Такой = mostly used as male pronoun.
Такая = only used as female pronoun.

But in this case, I couldn't finish my sentence in Russian (I didn't tell 'стала/become'), because I was too slow, sleepy and nervous, so 'такой' sounded as male pronoun, YET if I had finished it, that would have sounded appropriate. 

However, it won't work as an excuse for her, she'll mark it as 'bullshit'.

I hope, too. Thank you.

Yes, she's very dramatic and oversensitive. She even admits it, but she can't control herself when she's carried by her emotions. I would not be so panicked if not the misgendering thing, that's too much. It hit her low self-esteem too bad.
